key_insight: Machine learning can diagnose simulated degradation mechanisms in lead-free RbSn₀.₅Ge₀.₅I₃ solar cells, but strong test scores do not guarantee generalization.
engineering_relevance: Replacing Spiro-OMeTAD with CuI raises simulated efficiency from 19.6% to 21.6%, mainly by improving fill factor.
method: Compare surrogate models trained on factorial grids and Latin hypercube samples.
Identify six degradation mechanisms with multi-label classification of temperature- and illumination-dependent open-circuit voltage.
evidence_signal: The classifier achieves macro F₁ = 0.938 versus 0.687 for a calibrated physics-rule baseline; grid-trained XGBoost falls from R² = 0.9997 on held-out grid points to 0.58 on independently sampled devices.
watch_item: The classifier fails to generalize to mechanism combinations absent from training, and experimental-device validation remains necessary.
paper_title: Interpretable machine learning diagnosis of degradation mechanisms in lead-free $RbSn_{0.5}Ge_{0.5}I_{3}$ solar cells from temperature- and illumination-dependent electrical measurements
